column3: BSB has “the Father” for γεννήσαντα (“the one who begot”) and “those born of Him” for the singular “the one begotten of Him.”
“Keep” renders ποιῶμεν (“do”).
Close to the Greek.
Close to the Greek.
BSB splits the question into a question and answer (“Only he who believes”).
BSB adds “to this.”
BSB follows the critical text: the words about three witnesses “in heaven: the Father, the Word, and the Holy Spirit, and these three are one” (the Textus Receptus) are absent.
BSB follows the critical text: “and there are three that testify on earth” (the Textus Receptus) is absent. “Are in agreement” renders “are into the one.”
“Even if” renders “if”; “human testimony” renders “the testimony of men.”
“Within him” renders “in himself.”
Close to the Greek.
Close to the Greek.
BSB follows the critical text, with no closing “and that you may believe in the name of the Son of God” (the Textus Receptus). BSB moves “to you who believe in the name of the Son of God” forward.
“Before Him” renders “toward Him.”
“Already possess what we have asked” renders “have the requests that we have asked.”
“He should ask God, who will give” recasts “he will ask, and He will give him life”; “this kind of sin” is added.
“Yet” renders “and.”
“Does not keep on sinning” renders the present “does not sin.” “Protects him” follows manuscripts that read “him”; the Greek here has “himself” (ἑαυτόν).
“Is under the power of” renders “lies in.”
Close to the Greek.
BSB follows the critical text with no “Amen”; it is in the Textus Receptus.
